**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence) satisfies the LICENSE rule at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **Affiliates and contractors** — § 13.1 grants rights directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," with Authorized Users permitted to exercise them. This is better than the fallback (which would only require Affiliates on written notice), as no notice condition applies.
- **Paid-up licences** — § 13.2 is "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid," with broad use/modify/derivative-works rights and contractor support.
- **Not revocable at will** — § 13.3 limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity. Walk-away territory (revocable at Vendor's discretion) is not present.
- **Successor transfer** — § 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under § 24, and § 24.1 allows Affiliate/M&A assignment without Vendor consent; § 24.4 further blocks Vendor from terminating, repricing or suspending on our change of control.
- **Definitions check** — "Affiliate" (§ 1.1) uses a standard >50%/management-control test, adequate for our group structure.

The only residual points are non-material and noted rather than flagged: the § 13.1 subscription grant runs for the subscription term (expected for hosted services), and Affiliate status lapses if the control relationship ends, which is customary.
